text: {"answerable": true, "answer": "Ordinary convolutional layers use a filter tensor defined on a regular grid, as with image pixels, video frames or audio. Atoms sit at arbitrary positions rather than on a grid, so such a filter tensor is not applicable [W2778051509#006][W2726670313#006]. Re-sampling onto a grid is possible, but choosing an interpolation scheme is hard and may need many grid points [W2726670313#006]. Discretizing would also lose the precise atom locations, which carry essential physical information [W2726670313#001]. A discrete filter cannot capture subtle positional changes, which gives discontinuous energy predictions [W2726670313#005]. SchNet therefore uses continuous-filter convolutions, in which a filter-generating neural network maps positions to filter values [W2778051509#006][W2726670313#006]."}
